name: Fort McHenry National Monument and Historic Shrine
author: parks-page-legacy
summary: Fort McHenry National Monument and Historic Shrine in Baltimore, Maryland, is the birthplace of the American national anthem. During the Battle of Baltimore on September 13–14, 1814, British naval forces bombarded the star-shaped fort for 25 hours during the War of 1812. The fort's successful defense inspired Francis Scott Key, who watched the bombardment from a truce ship in the harbor, to write the poem "Defence of Fort M'Henry," which was later set to music and became "The Star-Spangled Banner," officially adopted as the national anthem in 1931. Designated as a national park in 1925 and redesignated in 1939, Fort McHenry is the only unit in the National Park System designated both a national monument and a historic shrine.
